feature: Replace hand-built JWT/refresh-token sign-in with ASP.NET Core Identity (Dapper/QBuilder IUserStore, cookie sessions, Google via generic AddOAuth); one person = one company + one role; desktop/local mode signs in nothing.

findings.evidence: SwitchingOff_StopsSignInAndAnOpenSession_KeepsEverything_AndCanBeUndone asserts only that the account row survives (COUNT(*) = 1) and can be re-activated; no test starts a build or deploy as a teammate, switches them off, then checks the build/history still shows that person's name. BuildRecord (back-end/ShipRight.Server/Modules/Builds/BuildRecord.cs:31) has no initiator field either.
findings.description: R8 acceptance line 'Builds and deploys they started still show their name' has no test (and no build field carries the initiator), so history retention for switched-off people is unproven.

findings.evidence: CompleteAsync returns Redirect(SwitchedOffRedirect) when !user.IsActive; nothing calls CompleteAsync with an inactive user. The only related test, GoogleSignInTests.cs:108 ASwitchedOffPerson_IsStillFlaggedOff_SoTheSignInIsRefused, calls ResolveUserAsync directly and asserts the returned user is inactive, so it still passes if line 113 is deleted.
findings.description: R8 edge 'A switched-off person trying Google sign-in with the same email is also refused' is enforced only by an untested endpoint branch; the guard could break without any test failing.

findings.evidence: CancelledRedirect ('/login?error=google_cancelled') and the OnRemoteFailure handler (line 61) are never asserted; CloudApiPipelineTests.cs:643-645 only covers the 'not configured' branch returning google_failed, and no test drives a cancelled remote failure or checks the sign-in screen then shows a plain message while email/password still work.
findings.description: R3 acceptance 'If Google sign-in is cancelled or fails, the person returns to the sign-in screen with a plain message and can still use email and password' is only half-proven (failure via not-configured branch; cancellation and the return path untested).

findings.evidence: TeamPage renders loading (line 265), error-with-retry (267-278), empty (280-282) and success (284) states, but TeamPage.test.tsx only exercises success ('loads and lists the team for an Admin', line 88); the mocked getMock always resolves with one member.
findings.description: R9 acceptance 'The list shows loading, empty, error-with-retry and success states' is covered only for the success state.

findings.evidence: No test performs an action with the keyboard only (all interactions use fireEvent.click/change) and none asserts a visible label via getByLabelText; the sign-in form (LoginPage.test.tsx) is the same. UX-002 requires visible labels and full keyboard accessibility.
findings.description: Keyboard operability and visible-label requirements are untested on the team and sign-in forms (R9 acceptance 'Every action works with the keyboard only, and every field has a visible label').

findings.evidence: No component test exists for signup.tsx, forgot-password.tsx, reset-password.tsx or change-password.tsx; the auth test tree has only LoginPage.test.tsx, AuthGuard.test.tsx, AuthApi.test.ts and ApiService.test.ts.
findings.description: R12 acceptance 'The sign-in, register, reset and Google screens show loading, error and success states' is proven only for the sign-in screen; register/reset screens have no component tests.

findings.evidence: Teammate_SavedTwiceAtOnce_IsCreatedOnce and the invalid-field tests never force a failure mid-write; registration has such a proof (Register_WithATakenEmail..._AndLeavesNoCompany, line 102) but teammate creation and Google first sign-in (GoogleSignIn.cs:98-110) have no forced-failure test for the reliability NFR 'leaves no partial records'.
findings.description: The reliability check for a failed teammate creation / Google first sign-in (no company without a person, no person without a company) is not proven by a forced-failure test.

findings.evidence: The app-boots check is not set up in this project (no scripts/smoke/run.mjs), so no start-and-look probe opens the new routes (/api/team, /api/auth/providers, /api/auth/google/start) or reads data through the new cookie sign-in. state.json already records this as the advisory CHK-app-boots finding.
findings.description: The feature's new read addresses have not been looked at by a running-app probe.
